body:

[Lingnoi] Food for thought - I've been using Gemini to find a provider ….
AEon Solar (aeonsolar.com.au) presents several significant red flags and indications that it is either an unpolished draft/template site or an untrustworthy operation. A close examination of the website's content and structure reveals the following critical concerns:
1. Unfinished Template Artifacts ("Placeholder" Content)
The website is riddled with generic placeholder text and pre-packaged template stubs leftover from a default WordPress/ThemeForest build:
Fake Contact Details: The contact pages and header areas display placeholder numbers like 123-456-7890 or US numbers like (229) 555-0109 and dummy addresses (e.g., “Moon ave, New York 2024 NY USA”), rather than a legitimate Australian business address or local phone line.
Incoherent Categories & Dummy Team Profiles: The product categories feature bizarre anomalies like a "Music" category, and the team section uses stock placeholder profiles (such as a generic bio for a "Solar Energy Technician" named Brooklyn Simmons).
Unconfigured Templates: Multiple pages rely entirely on generic pre-built template layouts (eergx_template/home-3-onepage/, etc.) without customization.
2. Lack of Verified Industry Credibility
No Track Record or Independent Reviews: There are no verified independent customer reviews, Clean Energy Council (CEC) retailer accreditations, or substantive public footprints linking this exact domain to a licensed, active solar installation business in Australia.
Transparency Deficits: Legitimate Australian solar providers typically display their Clean Energy Council Approved Solar Retailer status, physical office locations, ABN/ACN corporate registry details, and direct local support lines prominently on their site—none of which are authentically provided here.
Verdict
aeonsolar.com.au displays the hallmarks of an abandoned setup, a placeholder domain, or a poorly constructed template site rather than a reliable, established local solar retailer.
If you are planning a residential or commercial solar/battery installation, it is strongly recommended to deal exclusively with established, CEC-accredited providers with verified physical track records, clear warranty backings, and transparent local customer reviews.

The Electric Viking, on YouTube, has had a couple of videos in the last couple of days regarding portable batteries (easily move from house to house) as well as Base batteries where you pay for the installation of their battery and then a monthly subscription of about $30month. That’s it, the battery will charge to full off peak and then put back into the grid in peak. Base make their money from the feedback into the grid.
So I’d be very hesitant to buy a battery at the present time, with these options only around the corner.
